sections.title: Cypriot endemic
sections.text: Morris squill is a small bulbous perennial found only in Cyprus, in moist, shaded crevices and woodland understory. Its flowering stems reach about 10–35 cm.

sections.title: Leaves and flowers
sections.text: It has three to six narrow, arching leaves up to 70 cm long and 0.5–1.5 cm wide. Each stem bears a loose cluster of one to five small star-shaped flowers, lilac or blue tinged with white. The plate’s blue flowers and basal leaves fit the documented range.

sections.title: Toxicity and protection
sections.text: IUCN’s Mediterranean Island Plants account reports Scilla species as toxic and places S. morrisii in Vulnerable status under its updated assessment. Do not eat it; it is also protected in Cyprus and listed in EU habitat legislation.
